title: Fixed Points in a Shuffle
problem: Eight distinct cards numbered 1 through 8 are uniformly shuffled into eight numbered positions. What is the expected number of cards that finish in the position matching their number?

hints.text: Consider each card separately rather than trying to count every possible number of matches.
Let Xi indicate that card i lands in position i. What is P(Xi = 1)?

solution.setup: For each i, let Xi equal 1 if card i occupies position i and 0 otherwise. The number of matches is X = X1 + ... + X8.
solution.reasoning: In a uniform shuffle, card i is equally likely to occupy any of the eight positions, so E[Xi] = P(Xi=1) = 1/8. Linearity gives E[X] = 8*(1/8). The match events are dependent, but that does not affect the calculation.
solution.sanityCheck: The same argument works for any positive number n of cards, producing n*(1/n)=1; small cases n=1 and n=2 agree.

keyInsight: A complicated dependent count can have a simple expectation when each possible contribution is considered separately.
recognitionCues: Expected number of matches suggests one indicator for each possible match.
commonMistakes: Attempting to enumerate derangements and every possible number of fixed points.
followUps: What is the expected number of cards within one position of their original position?

source.notes: Original wording of the classical fixed-points expectation family.

verification.notes: Each of eight fixed-point indicators has expectation 1/8; exhaustive enumeration is implemented in scripts/verify_answers.py.
